$comment: A2 estate change-amplification scenario. The mechanisms are taken from the two-host prototypes and extraction experiments; six-site values are explicit extrapolations, not observations of six production sites.

scenario.assumption: Each product consumes a versioned shared package or centrally delivered token stylesheet where the evaluated architecture supports one. A rebuild is counted separately from a source edit.

changes.token: Change one shared colour, typography or spacing value.
changes.interactionPolicy: Change one shared component behaviour or accessibility policy needed by all six products.
changes.upstreamUpgrade: Upgrade the candidate foundation without changing product requirements.

react-aria.basis: measured mechanism, modelled at six sites
react-aria.notes: The records capability is consumed by both hosts from one package. The six-site model assumes the same governed foundation is adopted by both product-system halves.

token.evidence: Live UNDRR custom-property references remain in shipped CSS; both hosts inherit a token-sheet change.

interactionPolicy.evidence: Filtering, sorting, pagination and announcement policy have one shared implementation consumed by both hosts.

upstreamUpgrade.evidence: The model places the React Aria dependency behind one governed foundation; breadth beyond the measured records capability remains a pilot assumption.

mui.basis: measured package, modelled across two parallel stacks
mui.notes: The MUI integration is shared, but Mangrove remains a separate component system. Estate-wide policy therefore has two authoritative implementations.

token.evidence: One UNDRR token source feeds both paths, but MUI resolves mapped values into bundles while Mangrove consumes its own path.

interactionPolicy.evidence: The shared MUI integration and the Mangrove component stack must implement the same policy separately.

upstreamUpgrade.evidence: The extracted MUI package centralises the suite dependency; only the three modelled data products consume that upgrade.

antd.basis: measured package, modelled across two parallel stacks
antd.notes: Ant Design was tested shared-first, but the application and Mangrove paths still express policy through different component systems.

token.evidence: One UNDRR token source feeds both paths, while Ant Design theme values are bundled into the data products.

interactionPolicy.evidence: The shared Ant integration and Mangrove must implement and validate the policy independently.

upstreamUpgrade.evidence: The shared Ant package centralises the suite dependency for the three modelled data products.

mantine.basis: architecture model; package propagation not measured
mantine.notes: A shared theme is feasible, but no cross-host extraction drill was completed and the two implementations currently differ.

token.evidence: Mantine bakes theme values into each bundle; the absence of a measured shared package leaves consumer edit cost unproved.

interactionPolicy.evidence: Type A requires separate Mantine and Mangrove implementations; shared-package propagation was not measured.

upstreamUpgrade.evidence: Upgrade fan-out is modelled because the current pair was not extracted into one maintained package.

carbon.basis: architecture model; translation path not measured
carbon.notes: Carbon and Mangrove remain separate visual and component authorities, with an additional translation layer for cross-stack use.

token.evidence: The canonical token changes once, but both the Mangrove and Carbon routes need validation because evaluated Carbon coverage is incomplete.

interactionPolicy.evidence: Carbon, Mangrove and the proposed translation layer can each carry part of an estate-wide component policy.

upstreamUpgrade.evidence: A Carbon upgrade must be reconciled with the project theme and any Carbon-to-Mangrove translation path; extraction was not measured.
